title: Lesson 11: The End of Moore's Law & Chiplet Packaging — js-tools
desc: Silicon's physical limits (quantum tunnelling below 3nm, dark silicon), Dennard scaling's earlier death, chiplet design, 3D IC packaging with TSVs, and yield modelling (Poisson/Murphy). Verified with a real engine: a 600mm² monolithic die gives 90 per 300mm wafer at 56.55% yield, while 150mm² chiplets give 416 at 86.23% — 196.49 USD against 111.51 USD of silicon, 43% cheaper. But counting the interposer, per-die testing and assembly risk the real saving is 29%, and for a small 100mm² chip the chiplet version costs more than twice as much. Cross-die latency is quantified too: 30% remote accesses cost 1.9×, 5% only 1.15×.
